lessons.title: Language models
lessons.subtitle: Week 5: Generative AI
lessons.body:
Language models learn statistical patterns in sequences of text units and generate continuations. Fluent output can still contain incorrect information.

Offline practice: Compare a plausible invented answer with your own course notes and mark unsupported claims. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: Language models learn statistical patterns in sequences of text units and generate continuations. Fluent output can still contain incorrect information.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Tokens and context
lessons.subtitle: Week 5: Generative AI
lessons.body:
A token is a unit used to represent text, not necessarily a whole word. Context is the input available for a response; context capacity varies by model.

Offline practice: Break a sentence into possible pieces and explain why this is only a tokenisation illustration. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Image and audio generation
lessons.subtitle: Week 5: Generative AI
lessons.body:
Generative systems can create images or audio as well as text. Generated media can misrepresent events or people, so origin and consent matter.

Offline practice: Draft a text description of an educational diagram without depicting a real private person. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Hallucinations
lessons.subtitle: Week 5: Generative AI
lessons.body:
A hallucination is generated content that is inaccurate or unsupported, including invented references. Asking for a citation does not guarantee a real source.

Offline practice: Inspect three invented citations and write how you would check whether they exist. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

lessons.title: Useful boundaries
lessons.subtitle: Week 5: Generative AI
lessons.body:
Generative tools can help with drafts and alternatives, while humans check facts and suitability. For a known answer, a reliable document may be more useful than generation.

Offline practice: Choose between a textbook, a calculator, and an AI draft for three learning tasks and justify each choice. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: Generative tools can help with drafts and alternatives, while humans check facts and suitability. For a known answer, a reliable document may be more useful than generation.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
